challenge_payload.title: Hello-ESP
challenge_payload.description:
Hello-ESP
You've recovered a mysterious .bin firmware labeled "hello-esp".
It appears to be designed for the ESP32 platform, but no source code is available.
Your objective is simple: flash it, monitor its behavior, and recover the flag.
Use esptool.py

challenge_payload.title: The Wired
challenge_payload.description:
The Wired — ESPILON Fleet Investigation
Something was interrupted.
The agents are still flashed. The link is broken. The devices continue to boot, identify themselves, and wait for instructions they never receive.
You've gained access to a machine that was once used to administer a fleet of ESP32-based agents. Logs, firmware dumps, technical notes — everything is still there.
The coordination point is still listening.
If you can understand how the agents communicate, prove your identity, and complete the handshake — the coordinator will tell you what it knows.
Ports:
- 1337 : Navi Shell (investigation)
- 2626 : C2 Coordinator

Accela Signal -- Chirp Spread Spectrum Decoder
During the KIDS experiment, Tachibana Labs deployed a covert LoRa-like mesh network throughout the hospital infrastructure. Code-named "Accela Signal", these transmissions use Chirp Spread Spectrum modulation to carry data fragments below the detection threshold of conventional receivers.
Your NAVI has intercepted the baseband IQ stream from one of these nodes. The signal contains chirp-modulated frames with encoded data. Analyze the modulation, demodulate the chirps, decode the protocol, and extract the hidden message.
Hint: The stream banner tells you the basics. The rest is signal processing.
